status_summary: Executive Order 14167 (signed 2025-01-20, published 2025-01-30) directed the Defense Department to assign U.S. Northern Command a mission of sealing the borders and repelling unlawful entry and trafficking. By 2025-06-11 the Associated Press reported that troops were detaining people accused of trespassing in national defense areas in New Mexico, with a second area in western Texas, and handing them to Border Patrol, and that more than 1,400 people had been charged with entering militarized areas; a New Mexico judge dismissed more than 100 of the national security charges. The sources do not describe National Guard participation in border arrests.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14167 directed Northern Command to be assigned a border sealing mission and the Defense Department to assess options to protect against mass unlawful entry and transnational criminal organizations.

The Associated Press reported that troops had begun detaining people accused of trespassing in national defense areas on the southern border in New Mexico and briefly holding them until Border Patrol took custody.

title: Use military and National Guard personnel in southwest border arrest operations
uncertainties: The documents designating the national defense areas were not located; a Federal Register API search for the sealing-mission memorandum returned no documents, so the designations rest on the news report. Developments after June 2025, including later court rulings on the trespass charges and any National Guard arrest role, were not found in a search. The recommendation sits in the DOJ chapter but is carried out mainly by the Defense and Homeland Security departments.
